title: Burst recovery pathways — latency & cost walkthrough
body:
Purpose
---
Quick walkthrough of 'recovery pathways' when a serving node (or slot pool) becomes unavailable during high concurrency bursts. This is a working memo aimed at: engineering (platform + runtime), observability, and product optimize to align on what we measure and what tradeoffs to present to customers. Not a canonical benchmark suite — exploratory notes with charts-in-text and concrete next-step experiments.

High level summary
---
- Two common recovery pathways we observed under simulated node loss during spikes: graceful degradation (shed sessions, reduce concurrency, continue on degraded latency) and model fallback (route to CPU/quantized variant or larger model in another region).
- Graceful-degradation maintains cost but raises per-query latency p95/p99 by 1.6–3x for 30–90s; model-fallback increases cost by 10–40% but keeps p95 closer to baseline for short windows.
- For most interactive SLAs (p95 < 250ms target), fallback to a quantized variant on nearby capacity + temporary session-shed policy is the preferred default.

Test matrix (quick)
---
- Hardware baseline: 8xA100-GPU pool (V100-equivalent configs for older tests), 2x 32-core control plane workers.
- Models: open-llama-30b (fp16), open-llama-30b-8bit (int8 quantized), sd-small-7b (fallback small model).
- Traffic shapes: sustained ramp (linear 0->1000 qps over 5m), microburst (0->1200 qps in 3s sustain 12s), cascaded node drop (N-1 node killed at peak).
- Policies: 1) Graceful-degrade (slot shed, queue depth limit), 2) Immediate-fallback (route to quantized variant), 3) Regional-fallback (route to different region with +50ms RTT).
- Observed metrics: median, p95, p99 latency (ms), cost-per-query ($), tokens/sec per-GPU, queue-depth, KV cache hit-rate.

Representative timeline (microburst + node-loss)
---
Time axis (s) relative to burst start:
 0s   : baseline 200 qps, stable p95=120ms, p99=240ms
 +3s  : client ramp hit 1200 qps, autoscaler reacts (scale decisions at t=+6s)
 +8s  : node A killed (simulated), 2/8 GPUs removed from pool
 +8s..+20s: recovery window (or fallback active)
 +30s : autoscaler either finished adding capacity or routes completed

ASCII latency sketch (p95) by pathway (numbers are median across 5 runs):
- Graceful-degrade:
   0s  120ms |====== baseline ======|
   8s  360ms |======== spike after node loss ========|  (p95 up ~3x)
   20s 210ms |--- partial recover --|
   30s 140ms |-- back to near baseline --|

- Immediate-fallback (quantized instance):
   0s  120ms |====== baseline ======|
   8s  160ms |--- small increase due to routing + quant penalty --|  (p95 up ~1.3x)
   20s 130ms |-- near baseline with slightly higher variance --|

- Regional-fallback (+50ms RTT) :
   0s 120ms |====== baseline ======|
   8s 175ms |--- RTT + cold-transfer cost --|
   25s 140ms |-- stabilizes after routing and cache warm --|

Numeric snapshot (median across runs)
---
Scenario: microburst, N-1 node kill at peak, model=open-llama-30b (fp16)
- Baseline (no node loss): p50=95ms, p95=120ms, p99=240ms, cost/query= $0.0125
- Graceful-degrade: p50=120ms, p95=360ms, p99=820ms, cost/query = $0.0118 (-5%): throughput drops 18% during window
- Quantized-fallback (immediate): p50=110ms, p95=156ms, p99=310ms, cost/query = $0.0140 (+12%): tokens/sec per GPU +7% due to int8 perf
- Regional-fallback: p50=130ms, p95=175ms, p99=380ms, cost/query = $0.0135 (+8%): cross-region cost + egress

Cost vs SLA tradeoff (short note)
---
- If product tier requires p95 < 250ms during 95% of windows, graceful-degrade fails the SLA for 50–90s windows in this config. Fallback to quantized variant meets SLA at ~+12% cost but requires model-variant compatibility and pre-warmed slots.
- Egress/regional-fallback looks attractive when local capacity is exhausted and quantized variants are unavailable, but note the added tail variability and potential security/region constraints for Private deployments.

KV cache & session-affinity notes
---
- KV cache hit-rate drops by ~45% immediately after node loss for grace-degrade because session affinity dissolves; this drives the p99 tail.
- Quantized-fallback keeps a higher effective cache-hit-rate if the quantized variant shares the same session keyspace (we tested transparent kv mapping), reducing cold penalties.

Visual-ish microtable (text) — cost per 10k queries relative to baseline
---
Mode                | cost/10k | delta % | median p95 (ms)
Baseline (fp16)     | $125     | +0%     | 120
Graceful-degrade    | $118     | -5%     | 360
Quantized-fallback  | $140     | +12%    | 156
Regional-fallback   | $135     | +8%     | 175

Notes on experimental setup limitations
---
- Autoscaler decision latency heavily influences results; our current test cluster uses an aggressive 6s scale decision. Real customer clusters may have different settings.
- We used synthetic traffic with Poisson interarrival and a small fraction of long-tail token sequences (10% > 512 tokens). Real workloads with more long-turn dialogues will amplify degradation effects.
- Cold-starts for quantized instances were pre-warmed in some runs; if not pre-warmed, quantized-fallback shows worse p95 at t<12s.

Actionable recommendations (short)
---
1) Default policy: immediate quantized-fallback + limited session-shed for interactive SLAs. Requires: pre-warm budget, model-variant registry entry, routing table TTL ~2s.
2) Expose a policy knob in Console (per-customer): preferred_recovery = [graceful, quantized, regional] and prewarm_budget (slots).
3) Add a runbook page on Confluence summarizing instrumentation: events (node_loss), policy_actuation_time, cache_hit_ratio, observed p95 delta. Link: confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Burst+Recovery+Runbook
4) New benchmark: run a matrix where quantized variants are cold vs warm to measure 0–30s penalty; surface it in Optimize as a single-line tradeoff card.

Open questions / follow ups
---
- How often do customers prefer cost savings vs latency durability? We need product input to prioritize default policy. (ping @product-hosted-api)
- For Private deployments with strict region constraints, regional-fallback may be illegal; add policy validation to deployment templates.
- Should we offer an SLA-priced "pre-warm buffer" product for mission-critical tiers? Cost math above suggests ~+10–15% list price to guarantee p95 in node-loss windows.

Appendix: quick-run commands used (devkit)
---
- run load: ./devkit/loadgen --profile microburst --qps 1200 --model open-llama-30b --duration 60s
- kill node: ./devkit/ctl node kill --id node-a --at 8s
- collect traces: ./devkit/collect --trace-ids session_* --out traces/mar19

Slack notes & references
---
- See thread: #runtime-performance \"mar19 microburst node-drop runs\" (ts=1700000000) for raw logs and run ids.
- Related GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/812 (adds route-to-quantized policy hook).

Bottom line
---
We can meet stringent interactive p95 SLAs during node-loss windows by paying a modest cost premium (~10–15%) to route to quantized variants and invest in a small pre-warmed buffer. Graceful-degrade preserves cost but frequently violates p95 targets for interactive apps. Next experiments: cold quantized start penalty sweep; production-ish workload replay; per-tenant policy economics.

Author notes
---
Drafted while pairing with Diego; Hannah ran the quantized perf runs and Samir validated cost model mapping. Will convert to a one-pager for Console UX team if we converge on default policy.
